hypothesis.title: product-catalog 2.0.3 rollout causes slow product listing and timeouts
hypothesis.summary: Product-catalog was deployed to version 2.0.3 at -17m. Immediately after, its p95 latency jumped from 18ms to 1021ms and it began logging "context deadline exceeded while listing products" errors (530 occurrences). This latency propagated upstream to frontend, causing frontend's p95 to rise from 187ms to 1682ms and triggering the alert. PostgreSQL metrics remain healthy (4ms p95, stable CPU), ruling out datastore degradation.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend p95 latency exceeding 1s. Traces show that product-catalog is the origin of the added latency (+1497ms in frontend traces, +950ms in product-catalog's own traces). Product-catalog's p95 latency jumped from 18ms to 1021ms at -15m, and frontend's p95 followed from 187ms to 1682ms. The error logs show 530 instances of "context deadline exceeded while listing products" in product-catalog, first seen at -17m. Three deployments occurred: product-catalog 2.0.2→2.0.3 at -17m, frontend at -8m, and currency at -4m. The product-catalog deploy timing (-17m) aligns precisely with when its latency spiked (-15m) and errors began (-17m). Product-catalog is on the failing path (frontend→product-catalog), and its symptoms started immediately after its own deploy. PostgreSQL, product-catalog's dependency, shows healthy metrics: p95 latency stable at 4ms, CPU at 12%, no error rate increase. The frontend and currency deploys are red herrings—frontend's deploy happened 9 minutes after product-catalog's symptoms began, and currency is not on the failing trace path. The mechanism is a bad deploy in product-catalog that introduced slow database queries or inefficient product listing logic, causing timeouts.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Product-catalog rolled out 2.0.2→2.0.3 at -17m, precisely when errors and latency began, establishing temporal causality.
530 ERROR logs 'context deadline exceeded while listing products' first seen at -17m confirm product-catalog is timing out on its core operation immediately after deploy.
Product-catalog p95 latency spiked from 18ms to 1021ms at -15m, a 56× increase, showing the service itself became slow after the deploy.
Traces attribute 100% of added frontend latency (+1497ms) to product-catalog, confirming it is the origin, not a victim.
PostgreSQL p95 remains stable at 4ms with no spike, ruling out datastore degradation and confirming the fault is in product-catalog's new code.
Frontend deployed at -8m, 9 minutes after product-catalog symptoms began at -17m, so it is a red herring and not the root cause.

suggested_actions.title: Rollback product-catalog to version 2.0.2
suggested_actions.rationale: The 2.0.3 deploy introduced the latency and errors. Rolling back to the last known good version (2.0.2) should immediately restore p95 latency to ~18ms and eliminate timeouts.

suggested_actions.title: Inspect product-catalog 2.0.3 code changes for inefficient queries
suggested_actions.rationale: Review the diff between 2.0.2 and 2.0.3 for changes to product listing logic, database queries, or ORM usage that could cause the 56× latency increase. Look for N+1 queries, missing indexes, or removed query limits.

suggested_actions.title: Scale product-catalog replicas to reduce per-instance load temporarily
suggested_actions.rationale: If rollback is not immediately feasible, scaling out may reduce per-instance request rate and mitigate timeout frequency, though it won't fix the underlying inefficiency.

alternatives.why_less_likely: PostgreSQL's own metrics are healthy: p95 latency stable at 4ms, CPU at 12%, no error rate increase. Postmortem PM-2026-06-17 shows that when PostgreSQL degrades, its own latency metrics spike. Here they do not, so the fault is in product-catalog's new code, not the database.
